Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 71, verse 5–20:

﴿He said: "My Lord, I have called my people night and day"﴾. Regarding this, there are two interpretations:

First: My calling them was so that they would worship You night and day.

Second: I called them, night and day, to Your worship.

﴿But my calling only increased them in flight﴾. This may bear two meanings:

First: they only increased in fleeing from Your obedience.

Second: fleeing from my summons to Your worship.

Qatadah said: It has reached me that a man would take his son to Noah, and say to his son: "Beware of this man, let him not deceive you, for my father took me to him and I was like you, and he warned me as I am warning you."

﴿And whenever I called them, that You might forgive them﴾, meaning: whenever I called them to faith, that You might forgive them what preceded of shirk.

﴿They put their fingers in their ears﴾, so that they would not hear his call, in order to despair him of an answer to what they did not hear. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He was forbearing and patient.

﴿And they covered themselves with their garments﴾, that is, they covered their heads and disguised themselves so that he would not recognise them.

﴿And persisted﴾ (wa-asarru): regarding this there are three interpretations. First: it is their remaining upon disbelief. Qatadah said: "Quduman qudumā" (pressing forward) in the disobedience of God, through their heedlessness of the fear of God, until the command of God came upon them.

Second: iṣrār (persistence) is to commit the sin deliberately, as said by al-Hasan.

Third: its meaning is that they remained silent about their sins and did not seek forgiveness, as said by al-Suddi.

﴿And they became arrogant, with great arrogance﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

First: that this is their disbelief in God and their denial of Noah, as said by al-Dahhak.

Second: that this is their abandoning of repentance, as said by Ibn Abbas. And his saying "istikbaran" (great arrogance) is an intensification.

﴿Then indeed I called them openly﴾, that is, with open proclamation such that some of them could see others.

﴿Then indeed I announced to them﴾, meaning the call. Mujahid said: its meaning is I cried out loud.

﴿And I spoke to them in private, in private﴾. The calling was secret for some of them from others. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

First: he called them at one time in secret and at another time openly.

Second: he called some of them in secret and some of them openly. All of this was from Noah, as an exaggeration in calling and gentleness in invitation.

﴿So I said: "Seek forgiveness of your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving"﴾. This contains encouragement to repentance. Hudhayfah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Seeking forgiveness is an erasure of sins." Al-Fudayl said: the servant says "astaghfaru Allah" (I seek God's forgiveness); he said: and its explanation is "aqallani" (may He lift me up/relieve me).

﴿He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾, meaning continuous rain. It was said that they had suffered drought for forty years, until the drought took away their wealth and the children ceased from their wives. So he said this as an encouragement to faith.

﴿And provide you with wealth and children, and make for you gardens and make for you rivers﴾. Qatadah said: the Prophet of God Noah knew that they were people greedy for this world, so he said: "Come to the obedience of God, for in His obedience is the attainment of this world and the Hereafter."

﴿What is the matter with you that you do not attribute to God [any] dignity (waqaran)?﴾ Regarding this there are five interpretations. First: "What is the matter with you that you do not recognise the greatness of God," said by Mujahid and Ikrimah.

Second: you do not fear the punishment of God and hope from Him for reward, said by Ibn Abbas in the narration of Ibn Jubayr.

Third: you do not recognise the right of God nor thank Him for His blessings, said by al-Hasan.

Fourth: you do not render to God obedience, said by Ibn Zayd.

Fifth: that waqar means steadfastness, and from it is the words of the Exalted: ﴿And remain in your houses﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33], that is, remain steadfast; and its meaning is: you do not affirm the oneness of God and that He is your God, besides whom there is no god for you. Ibn Bahr said: He guided them to this when He said: ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

First: meaning a stage of being a drop of sperm, then a stage of a clinging clot, then a stage of a lump of flesh, then a stage of bone; then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation, causing hair to grow for him and the form to be completed for him, said by Qatadah.

Second: that the stages (atwar) are their variation in height and shortness, strength and weakness, concern and activity, wealth and poverty.

It may also bear a third meaning: that the stages are their variation in character and deeds.

﴿Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers?﴾ Regarding this there are two statements:

First: that they are seven heavens above seven earths, with creation between each heaven and earth; this is the saying of al-Hasan.

Second: that they are seven heavens in layers, some above others, like domes; this is the saying of al-Suddi.

﴿And made the moon therein a light﴾. Regarding this there are two statements:

First: its meaning is that He made the moon therein a light for the people of the earth, said by al-Suddi.

Second: that He made the moon therein a light for the people of the heaven and the earth, said by Ata.

Ibn Abbas said: its face shines for the people of the earth, and its back shines for the people of the heaven.

﴿And made the sun a lamp﴾, meaning a lamp for the people of the earth; regarding its relation to the people of the heaven, the two earlier statements apply.

﴿And God has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: meaning that He created Adam from the surface of the whole earth, said by Ibn Jurayj. Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: man was created from clay, and hearts soften only in winter.

Second: that He caused them to grow from the earth, by greatness after smallness, and by height after shortness, said by Ibn Bahr.

Third: that the whole of creation was brought into being by nourishment from what the earth produces and what is in it; and this is a possibility.

﴿Then He will return you into it﴾, meaning as dead in the graves.

﴿And bring you forth [again], a bringing forth﴾ for resurrection by the Resurrection.

﴿And God has made the earth for you a spread-out expanse﴾, that is, spread out; and in this is evidence that it is spread out.

﴿That you may follow therein roads, wide pathways﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: differing paths, said by Ibn Abbas.

Second: wide paths, said by Ibn Kamil.

Third: paths marked out with signs, said by Qatadah.

Second: you do not fear the punishment of God and hope from Him for reward, said by Ibn Abbas in the narration of Ibn Jubayr.

Third: you do not recognise the right of God nor thank Him for His blessings, said by al-Hasan.

Fourth: you do not render to God obedience, said by Ibn Zayd.

Second: that the stages (atwar) are their variation in height and shortness, strength and weakness, concern and activity, wealth and poverty.

It may also bear a third meaning: that the stages are their variation in character and deeds.

First: that they are seven heavens above seven earths, with creation between each heaven and earth; this is the saying of al-Hasan.

Second: that they are seven heavens in layers, some above others, like domes; this is the saying of al-Suddi.

First: its meaning is that He made the moon therein a light for the people of the earth, said by al-Suddi.

Second: that He made the moon therein a light for the people of the heaven and the earth, said by Ata.

Second: that He caused them to grow from the earth, by greatness after smallness, and by height after shortness, said by Ibn Bahr.

Third: that the whole of creation was brought into being by nourishment from what the earth produces and what is in it; and this is a possibility.

﴿Then He will return you into it﴾, meaning as dead in the graves.

﴿And bring you forth [again], a bringing forth﴾ for resurrection by the Resurrection.

﴿And God has made the earth for you a spread-out expanse﴾, that is, spread out; and in this is evidence that it is spread out.

First: differing paths, said by Ibn Abbas.

Second: wide paths, said by Ibn Kamil.

Third: paths marked out with signs, said by Qatadah.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 71, verse 21–24:

﴿Nuh said: "My Lord, they have disobeyed me.﴾ The people of tafsir said: he remained among them for what Allah has told of, a thousand years less fifty years, calling them while they persisted in their disbelief and rebellion. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Nuh hoped for children after fathers, so they would bring him child after child, until they reached seven generations. Then he prayed against them after despairing of them, and he lived after the Flood sixty years, until the people multiplied and spread.

al-Hasan said: The people of Nuh used to sow twice a month.

﴿And they followed one whose wealth and children increase him only in loss.﴾ It is recited "waladuhu" with a fatha on the waw and with a damma on it, and on both there are two opinions:

The first: that "al-walad" with a damma is a group of children, and "al-walad" with a fatha is one of them. This was said by al-Aʿmash. al-Rabiʿ ibn Ziyad said:

"And if your war has become a mutual affair, I was not among those who committed it.
But the sons of Sawda kindled it, and fed its fire for whoever warms himself at it."

﴿And they schemed a great scheme﴾ meaning a great one. al-Kubbar is a stronger intensive than kabir.

On it there are two aspects. The first: what they attributed to Allah of partners and children. This was said by al-Kalbi.(p-104)

The second: it is the saying of their leaders to their followers: ﴿And they said: Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd or Suwaʿ﴾ (the verse), as said by Muqatil.

Regarding these idols there are two opinions:

The first: that they belonged to the Arabs and no one else worshipped them. The meaning of the speech is: just as the people of Nuh said to their followers "Do not leave your gods," the Arabs said likewise to their children and their people: "Do not leave Wadd, nor Suwaʿ, nor Yaghuth, Yaʿuq, or Nasr." Then the mention returned after that to the people of Nuh.

These names have been differed over. ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: Adam fell ill, and with him were his sons: Wadd, Suwaʿ, Yaghuth, Yaʿuq and Nasr; and Wadd was the greatest of them and the most dutiful to him. Others said: these names belonged to men before the people of Nuh. When they died, their children grieved over them a severe grief, so Satan adorned for them that they should make their images so that they could look at them, and they did so. Then their children worshipped them after them.

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: They were righteous people between Adam and Nuh, then after them there arose those who took up worship in their manner. Iblis adorned for them that they should fashion their forms so that by them they would remember their striving. Then the people of Nuh worshipped them after them, then they passed on after them to the Arabs, and the descendants of Ismaʿil worshipped them.

As for Wadd, it was the first idol worshipped. It was named so for their love (wudd) of it. After the people of Nuh it was for the tribe of Kalb at Dawmat al-Jandal, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtaʾ and Muqatil. Concerning it their poet says:

"May Wadd greet you, for it is not lawful for us
the play of women, and the religion has resolved."

As for Suwaʿ, it was for Hudhayl on the sea coast, according to them. As for Yaghuth, it was for Ghatif of Murad in al-Jawf of Saba, according to Qatada. Muqatil said: a clan of Najran.

Abu ʿUthman al-Nahdi said: I saw Yaghuth, and it was of lead, and they used to carry it on a bare-backed camel, and they would travel with it without provoking it, until it was the one that knelt down. When it knelt, they dismounted and said: "It has approved the resting place for you," and they would build a structure upon it and settle around it.

As for Yaʿuq, it was for Hamdan at Balkh, according to Qatada, ʿIkrima and ʿAtaʾ.(p-105)

As for Nasr, it was for Dhu al-Kalaʿ of Himyar, according to ʿAtaʾ, and similarly from Muqatil.

The first: he means that many of his people were led astray by these idols.

The second: that the great ones of his people led many of their juniors and followers astray.

The second: one who inhabits dwellings. This was said by al-Suddi.

﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ regarding this there are two views:

One of them: he meant his father, whose name was Lamak, and his mother, whose name was Minjal, and both were believers. This was said by al-Hasan.

The second: he meant his father and his grandfather. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

﴿And whoever enters my house as a believer﴾ regarding this there are three aspects:

One of them: he means my friend who enters my home. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: whoever enters my mosque. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The third: whoever enters my religion. This was said by Juwaybir.

﴿And for the believing men and believing women﴾ regarding this there are two views:

One of them: he meant from among his people.

The second: from all of creation until the Hour is established. This was said by al-Dahhak.

﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers﴾ meaning the disbelievers.

﴿except in ruin﴾ (tabaran) regarding this there are two aspects:

One of them: destruction.

The second: loss. Both were related by al-Suddi.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 71, verse 25–28:

﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dweller."﴾ The scholars differed regarding the cause of Noah's supplication against his people with this, on two views:

One of them: When there was revealed to him the words of the Most High: ﴿None will believe among your people except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36], he supplicated against them with this supplication. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: A man from his people carried his young son on his shoulder, and passed by Noah, and said to his son: "Beware of this one, for he will mislead you."
